about: cesr.parse cases for primitives of each code size. A stream must start with a count code, an op code, a field map or annotated text, never a bare primitive, so each stream opens with the genus/version code -_AAACAA and carries its primitives in a generic list group (-J), which the master table defines for mixed types.

cases.title: Parse one Ed25519 verification key in a list group
cases.description: A genus/version code, then a -J group of 11 quadlets holding one 44-character D primitive. The decoder must report the key's code and raw value at its offsets.

cases.title: Parse primitives with one-, two- and four-character codes
cases.description: One -J group holding a D key (1-character code, 44 characters), a 0B signature (2-character code, 88), a 1AAB secp256k1 key (4-character code, 48) and a 0A salt (2-character code, 24). The group is 51 quadlets.

cases.title: Parse primitives with one-, two- and four-character codes in the binary domain
cases.description: The stream of CESR-0013 entirely in the binary domain. Offsets are bytes, and the -J size is the same 51, now counting triplets.

cases.title: Parse variable-size byte strings with zero, one and two lead bytes
cases.description: Byte strings of 9, 8 and 7 bytes need 0, 1 and 2 lead bytes to reach a multiple of 3, so they take the codes 4B, 5B and 6B, each with a size of 3 quadlets in its last two code characters. The raw value reported excludes the lead bytes.

cases.title: Parse an Ed448 signature with a four-character code
cases.description: Code 1AAE, a 114-byte signature with pad size 0, 156 characters, in a -J group of 39 quadlets.
